title: "Storage Full" on Your Phone
youtube_title: Phone Says "Storage Full"? Here's How to Fix It | Fix It Friday
next: Next Friday: My Computer Won't Turn On
description: Can't take a photo because your storage is full? Kip and Bub show how to find what's using the space on iPhone and Android, and the safest ways to free it up without losing your photos.

scenes.say: Your phone says storage is full. You can't take a photo, and updates won't install. Let's fix it.
It's Fix It Friday. Today: what to do when your phone says storage is full.
Phones fill up with four things: photos and videos, apps, messages with pictures and videos attached, and downloaded files.

First, see what's actually using the space. On an iPhone, open Settings, then General, then iPhone Storage. On most Android phones, open Settings, then Storage. You'll see a bar showing what's taking up room.

card.title: Step 1: See what is using space

scenes.say: Photos and videos are usually the biggest. Turn on a cloud backup, like iCloud Photos or Google Photos, so your pictures are saved safely online. On iPhone, the Optimize iPhone Storage option then keeps smaller copies on the phone. In Google Photos, Free up space removes copies that are already backed up.

card.title: PHOTOS: back up, then slim down

scenes.say: Just make sure the backup has finished first. And videos are the real space hogs. A single minute of video can take up as much room as dozens of photos, so delete the ones you don't need.

card.text: Check the backup finished before deleting.

scenes.say: Next, apps. Remove the ones you haven't opened in months. On iPhone, Offload Unused Apps removes the app but keeps your data, so you can reinstall it later. Many Android phones can archive unused apps the same way.

card.title: APPS: remove what you don't use

scenes.say: Messages add up too. Long conversations full of photos and videos can take gigabytes. On iPhone, the Messages settings let you keep messages for one year instead of forever.

card.sub: iPhone: keep messages 1 year, not forever

scenes.say: Finally, restart the phone. It clears out temporary files the phone has been holding onto.
So: check what's using space, back up and slim down your photos, remove unused apps, trim old messages, and restart.
Got a tech problem you want fixed? Leave it in the comments, and it might be a future Fix It Friday. See you next Friday.
